## How it works

- [statement] Lo, Mamaysky and Wang (2000) report incremental information in several technical indicators when comparing conditional and unconditional daily US stock return distributions. (low confidence) — https://web.mit.edu/wangj/www/pap/LoMamayskyWang00.pdf
- [statement] Cont-Kukanov-Stoikov report approximately linear short-horizon price impact of order-flow imbalance with depth-dependent slope in their US equity sample. (low confidence) — https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1011.6402
- [statement] Huang-Lehalle-Rosenbaum model order-flow intensities as functions of current order-book state during periods of constant reference price. (low confidence) — https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1312.0563
- [statement] Both Huang-Lehalle-Rosenbaum and Albers et al. explicitly include queue state and order priority or position when analyzing passive execution outcomes. (medium confidence) — https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1312.0563 · keywords: Market Graph Geometry and Strategy Regime Efficacy · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2
- [statement] Chávez-Casillas-Figueroa-López show in their LOB description that touch depletion and, when the spread exceeds one tick, new orders inside the spread are distinct mechanisms for changes in best quotes. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/1407.5684v3
- [statement] Cont, Kukanov and Stoikov report a short-interval approximately linear association between order-flow imbalance and price changes, with impact slope inversely related to depth. (low confidence) — https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1011.6402
- [statement] Huang, Lehalle and Rosenbaum model order-flow intensities as functions of current book state within constant-reference-price intervals. (low confidence) — https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1312.0563

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Ruiz-Ortiz et al. report that their average turbulence index generally peaks after the studied crashes start and can lag slow declines. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2203.05603

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Sanchez Garcia and Gherghe argue that their studied Ollivier-Ricci construction is an ex-post crisis descriptor rather than an indicator of tendencies toward a crisis. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07134

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Lo, Mamaysky and Wang (2000) and Savin, Weller and Zvingelis (2006 manuscript) use algorithmic technical-pattern recognition based on kernel regression in US equity studies. (low confidence) — https://web.mit.edu/wangj/www/pap/LoMamayskyWang00.pdf · keywords: Market Graph Geometry and Strategy Regime Efficacy · also: https://www.biz.uiowa.edu/faculty/gsavin/papers/hsrevision_paw_10%2019%2006.pdf
- [statement] Kim, Koh, Boyd and Gorinevsky (2009) explicitly describe l1 trend filtering as a batch method estimating a trend from the whole history of observations. (low confidence) — https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/pdf/l1_trend_filter.pdf
- [statement] Kim, Koh, Boyd and Gorinevsky (2009) state that l1 trend filtering produces piecewise-linear trend estimates and interpret slope changes as possible changes or events in underlying dynamics. (low confidence) — https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/pdf/l1_trend_filter.pdf
- [statement] For S&P 500 stocks in 1990–1999, Savin, Weller and Zvingelis report no evidence that a stand-alone head-and-shoulders trading strategy would be profitable; their corresponding Russell 2000 evidence is weak. (low confidence) — https://www.biz.uiowa.edu/faculty/gsavin/papers/hsrevision_paw_10%2019%2006.pdf
- [statement] Lo, Mamaysky and Wang report incremental conditional-return information for some algorithmically detected chart patterns, while explicitly distinguishing this from excess trading profits. (low confidence) — https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w7613/w7613.pdf
- [statement] Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen report return persistence at intermediate horizons with partial longer-horizon reversal in their August 2010 time-series momentum draft. (low confidence) — https://elmwealth.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/timeseriesmomentum.pdf
- [statement] Gidea-Katz and Ruiz-Ortiz et al. construct sliding-window point clouds and summarize persistent-homology features with persistence landscapes. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/1703.04385 · keywords: Market Graph Geometry and Strategy Regime Efficacy · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2203.05603
- [statement] In the historical samples examined by Sandhu et al. and Samal et al., average Ollivier-Ricci network curvature increased during crisis periods relative to normal periods. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/1505.05182 · keywords: Market Graph Geometry and Strategy Regime Efficacy · also: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/physics/articles/10.3389/fphy.2020.624373/full
- [statement] Ismail et al. choose their correlation threshold from values one day before the known Dotcom and Lehman crises, then apply it to all available dates. (low confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/applied-mathematics-and-statistics/articles/10.3389/fams.2022.940133/full
- [statement] Ismail et al. report Spearman MPS PSA 46.15 and PEA 53.85 (percentage values), with EWS=4, FA=7, FN=7 and TN=8 in their event classification. (low confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/applied-mathematics-and-statistics/articles/10.3389/fams.2022.940133/full
- [statement] Schreiber and Schmitz explain that rejection of a stationary linear surrogate null can be caused by nonlinearity or nonstationarity, and that nonlinearity alone does not establish deterministic chaos. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/chao-dyn/9909037
- [statement] Ruiz-Ortiz et al. write each point-cloud window as Z^t={z_t,...,z_(t+w-1)}, so a forward implementation must timestamp that window only after its last observation is available. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2203.05603
- [statement] Chabot, Ghysels and Jagannathan report time-varying momentum crash hazards in Victorian and CRSP-era data. (low confidence) — https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w20660/w20660.pdf
- [statement] Daniel and Moskowitz report that momentum crashes occur in panic states after declines and high volatility, and coincide with market rebounds. (low confidence) — https://kentdaniel.net/papers/published/jfe_16.pdf
- [statement] Gould-Bonart and Albers et al. both define top-of-book imbalance as bid quantity minus ask quantity divided by their sum. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.03492 · keywords: Market Graph Geometry and Strategy Regime Efficacy · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2
- [statement] Gould-Bonart report out-of-sample next-midprice classification gains in their Nasdaq sample; Albers et al. describe more common imbalance-aligned next-price cases than reversal cases in their Binance sample. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.03492 · keywords: Market Graph Geometry and Strategy Regime Efficacy · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2
- [statement] DeLise and Albers et al. both document adverse post-fill midprice drift for passive orders in their respective Treasury-futures simulation and Binance Bitcoin-perpetual experiment. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2407.16527v1 · keywords: Market Graph Geometry and Strategy Regime Efficacy · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2
- [statement] In the Albers live Binance experiment, naive two-sided maker quoting and the examined simple imbalance strategies perform poorly despite spread capture and rebates. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2
- [statement] Albers et al. state that a favorable imbalance can leave a maker order at the end of the longer queue with low fill probability, whereas taking liquidity pays the taker fee. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2
- [statement] Chávez-Casillas-Figueroa-López identify constant one-tick spread, fixed order volume and queue reset after depletion as restrictive assumptions, and propose preserving the un-depleted opposite queue with variable spread. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/1407.5684v3
- [statement] Gould and Bonart report one-tick-ahead predictive information from bid/ask queue imbalance, with stronger classification improvement for large-tick stocks. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.03492
